title: Visualization and quantification of the stromal-vascular compartment in fetal or adult mouse bones: From sampling to high-resolution 3D image analysis
protocol: Euthanize the pregnant dam at embryonic day E18.5 or the desired fetal age using CO2 inhalation.
Spray the surface of the abdomen region with 70% ethanol.
Make an incision in the fur and skin to access the peritoneal cavity.
Cut the peritoneal membrane to reach the abdominal cavity.
Lift the uterine horn at the ovarian side out of the abdominal cavity.
Cut at the level of the cervix to isolate the uterus.
Place the uterus into a pre-filled petri dish with PBS solution.
Clean the uterus from the mesometrium membrane.
Isolate the embryos by cutting the uterine horns and liberating them from the embryonic sac.
Remove extraembryonic tissues and organs.
Cut the umbilical blood vessels to remove the placenta.
Euthanize the isolated embryos according to local guidelines.
Immerse the isolated embryos in clean PBS in a second petri dish.
Sacrifice newborn pups using the appropriate prescribed method.
Rinse the pups with PBS.
Immerse the pups in clean PBS in a second petri dish.
Dissect embryonic and newborn mouse limbs in a clean petri dish with PBS using a stereoscopic microscope, small scissors, and a pair of fine tweezers.
Remove the skin and excess soft tissue/muscles from the dissected limbs.
Fix dissected limbs for 12–16 hours at 4°C in 2% PFA prepared in PBS.
Take off the PFA solution after fixation.
Wash samples with PBS three times, each for 5 minutes at room temperature with mild agitation.
Decalcify perinatal bones (E18.5 to P2 samples) in 0.5 M EDTA for two days at 4°C with daily renewed EDTA solution.
Wash decalcified samples with PBS three times, each for 5 minutes at room temperature with mild agitation.
Euthanize adult mice by CO2 inhalation in a glass desiccator.
Spray limbs with 70% ethanol.
Cut and retract the skin from the legs using scissors.
Remove muscles using scissors and tweezers.
Collect bones of interest.
For tibia and femur, cut the foot at the ankle using scissors.
Separate the tibia and femur by carefully cutting soft tissues/ligaments at the knee level.
Fix samples in 4% PFA in PBS for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Wash samples with PBS three times, each for 20 minutes with constant agitation.
Decalcify juvenile and adult samples in 0.5 M EDTA for two weeks at 4°C, changing the EDTA solution weekly.
Wash samples with PBS three times, each for 20 minutes with constant agitation.
Proceed with embedding protocol.
Pre-condition samples in cryoprotection medium, using approximately 2.5 mL per sample to fully cover the tissue.
Incubate the samples in the cryoprotection medium for 24 hours at 4°C.
Prepare gelatin embedding medium by adding 8% (w/v) of gelatin to the cryoprotection medium.
Stir gently until the gelatin is completely dissolved, avoiding air bubbles.
Label molds and fill them completely with warm (∼65°C) gelatin embedding medium.
Pour the medium gently into the molds to avoid bubbles.

Using tweezers, submerge the bone sample in the gelatin, positioning it centrally in the mold with the growth plate perpendicular to the vertical axis of the mold and the bone shaft leveled horizontally.
Let the samples cool down on the bench at 20°C–22°C for 15–30 minutes until the gelatin solidifies.
Store the blocks at -80°C.
Transfer tissue samples to labeled plastic molds.
Cover tissues with Optimal Cutting Temperature (OCT) compound.
Submerge a borosilicate glass recipient containing 2-methylbutane in liquid nitrogen.
Allow the bottom part of the 2-methylbutane solution to solidify and turn opaque white while the upper part remains fluidic.
Submerge the mold containing the tissue sample into the cold 2-methylbutane solution until it quickly freezes (takes around 10 seconds).
Remove the frozen tissue block from 2-methylbutane once completely solidified.
Place samples on dry ice until all are collected.
Store collected samples at -80°C.
Retrieve gelatin- or cryo-embedded blocks from −80°C.
Transfer the blocks to the cryostat at −20°C for temperature conditioning.
Trim excess gelatin or OCT compound using a blade or scalpel.
Mount the block into the cryostat chuck using OCT compound.
Place the chuck into the fast-freezing station inside the cryostat.
Cut ∼50 μm slices until the bone surface of the sample appears.
Redirect the sample holder in X, Y and Z to obtain even, longitudinal sections across the bone.
Cut tissue sections at the desired thickness.
Collect bone sections on coated adhesion microscope slides (e.g., Superfrost Plus).
For gelatin sections: Let the sections condition at 20°C–22°C for ∼30 minutes to ensure adhesion to the slide.
For cryo-sections: Ensure that the slides are at 20°C–22°C before sectioning to allow proper adherence.
Store the slides with bone sections at −80°C for long-term preservation.

Immunostain bone sections to detect blood vessels via endothelial cell antigens, identify skeletal stem/progenitor cells within the tissue stroma, and/or visualize GFP-expressing or EdU-containing proliferating cells as required.
Allow the slides to come to 20°C–22°C and dry for 1 hour to improve section adherence.
Incubate with PBS-T for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°C–22°C) to rehydrate the tissue.
Apply every solution gently during the procedure.
Clean excess cryo-embedding medium or gelatin remnants from around the bone section using a wipe or blade.
Draw a circle around the bone section using a hydrophobic pen.
Ensure tissue sections are immersed in water-based solutions during staining procedure.
Perform incubations in a humidified, closed chamber.
Keep sections protected from light when fluorescent signals are involved.
Block and permeabilize samples by adding 100 μL of Blocking Solution per section for 45 min at 20°C–22°C or 12–16 h at 4°C in a humid/moisture chamber.
Incubate samples with 100 μL of primary antibodies diluted in Blocking Solution for 12–16 h at 4°C (thin or relatively thick sections) or for 24 h (very thick sections and trimmed half bones).
Rinse samples briefly once.
Wash samples at least 3–4 times for 10 min each using PBS-T at RT.
Incubate samples with 100 μL of secondary antibodies diluted at 1:200 in PBS-T for 75 min at 20°C–22°C (for 2D imaging) or 24 h at 4°C (for 3D imaging).
Rinse samples briefly once.
Wash samples in PBS-T for 10 min at least 3–4 times at 20°C–22°C.
Incubate samples with 100 μL of Hoechst diluted at 1:500 (final concentration 20 μg/mL) for 10 min for thin sections and 30 min for thick sections and half bones at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse samples briefly once.
Wash samples in PBS-T for 10 min once at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse samples and incubate in 10% TDE in PBS for at least 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse samples and incubate in 25% TDE in PBS for at least 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse samples and incubate in 50% TDE in PBS for at least 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse samples and incubate in 95%-100% TDE for at least 1 h at 20°C–22°C (do not perform this step when using green fluorescent signals).
Mount the slides in 200 μL of TDE at the final concentration used in the clearing steps.
Slowly place the coverslip to avoid bubble formation.
If a bubble forms, tilt the slide vertically and re-fill the area under the coverslip with TDE using a micropipette.
Remove excess TDE by slightly pressing on top of the coverslip with a finger.
Seal the slides with nail polish.
Keep the slides at 4°C and image in the next few days.
Apply 3–4 drops of Fluoroshield mounting medium on top of the section.
Place the edge of the coverslip on a corner of the slide and move it towards the section until touching the mounting medium.
Carefully lower the coverslip into place and gently press using blunt-end tweezers to remove excess mounting medium.
Place a small amount of Vaseline in a petri dish and mold it into a rectangle large enough to hold the half bone.
Cut a square of parafilm as large as the Vaseline square and stretch it until thin and malleable.
Cover the Vaseline with the stretched parafilm carefully to avoid tearing it.
Place the half bone on top of the parafilm/Vaseline mold.
Put a Menzel-Gläser coverslip on top of the half bone.
Apply pressure on top of the coverslip delicately until the trimmed half bone side is horizontal and stable.
Recommend the use of laser-scanning confocal microscopy for imaging structures that require high levels of detail and resolution.
Recommend spinning disk confocal microscopy for organ-scale images.

Adjust the laser power, gain, and resolution for the desired image quality.

Gently place the slide on the bottom of the TDE-filled dish to avoid bubble formation.

Place the petri dish on the microscope stage.

Rotate the image in steps of 90° until a smaller angle is required using the “Image>Transform>Rotate 90 degrees to the Right/Left” tools.
